fair_value_reason: Agents' round-4 fair values are $190/$198/$159/$228/$198 (mean $194.5). Restated with the settled owned-site costs and the unnamed-GW treatment applied to each agent's DCF leg at its own weight, plus the net-debt effect of the changed facility capex on its multiples legs: agent_1 ~$178 (DCF $122, EV/sales ~$215), agent_2 ~$214 (DCF $149, EV/EBITDA ~$280), agent_3 ~$161 (DCF $105), agent_4 ~$218 (DCF $171, multiples -$3), agent_5 ~$176 (DCF $132, EV/sales ~$205). Mean ~$190, ~18% below spot. Reconciled DCFs alone: split ~$105-171 (mean ~$136), single ~$101-166 (mean ~$132).

thesis_triggers.event: Four agents sit at $115 and agent_4 at $120. $115 is below the $138.75 Sep-25 conversion price and near the low end of the reconciled DCFs at a 5-year life or steep re-lease path. A close there would most likely mean new-deal $/MW reverting toward the ~$12M fleet base, owned campuses (Highridge 260 MW by Oct-2027, Meta tranches from early 2027) slipping, or contract-secured financing failing to scale. Ordinary volatility is unlikely to explain it. The signed IG contracts (~$29-60/share net of build capex) are the floor beneath it.

supervisor_summary: Round 4 rebuilt every DCF from the 25-site inventory with split discounting. All five agents account for each site once with correct terms and payment direction, and anchor contract rates soundly on the verified SOFR+2.50% facility (7.5-9.0% investment-grade, at WACC outside the terms). The split adds only $3-5 because the contracts are short. The big swing was the cost of owned campuses: facility capex ranged from $7.5M to $16M per MW, worth +$1 to +$77 per agent. Settling it at ~$13M per utility MW (C&W 2026, JLL) and ~$1.45M/MW-yr all-in narrows the DCFs from $97-188 to ~$105-171 (single-rate ~$101-166). The restated fair value is ~$190, ~18% below spot. The ladder is trimmed by ~1 point (P>=$232 0.442), with low confidence.
key_drivers: Revenue per MW over a cohort's life (new-cohort price, the 5-year share, the re-lease path) is still the biggest lever: agent_3 launch price +/-$2M/MW gives $26-167; agent_2 glut vs supply-short gives $50-199; agent_5 relaunch $16M/$20M gives $131-225.

Owned-site economics, now settled at ~$13M facility capex per utility MW and ~$1.45M/MW-yr all-in running cost (C&W 2026 $17.6M/IT-MW excl. chips; JLL $11.3M shell-and-core). Each $1M/MW of facility cost moves the DCFs $5-13/share, and each $0.1M/MW-yr of running cost moves them ~$4-5. Owned sites hold ~3.1 GW, ~70-75% of expected MW.

Contract book: Microsoft $17.4B to mid-2031, Meta $2.9B plus $12B dedicated from early 2027, the backstop up to $15B, and Q2-26 deals over $4B. It is worth ~$29-60/share net of build capex at 7.5-9.0% (anchored on the SOFR+2.50% facility). The split rate adds only $3-5 because the terms are short.

Execution and funding of >1 GW/yr: Highridge 260 MW by Oct-2027, Independence additional power by early 2029, Birmingham lawsuits, the ~1 GW of the 5 GW target with no named site, and dilution toward ~380-400M shares.
The sector multiple (CoreWeave ~4-5x EV/NTM sales, ~8-9x forward EBITDA) carries 50-60% of every blended fair value.
